review: 302.1-1: the combat variant used a declare attackers step with no attackers, a step Forge may skip; moved it to the beginning of combat step.
302.5-2: the setup did not say Grizzly Bears could attack; stated it has been under A's control since the turn began.

scenarios.title: A creature can be cast only in a main phase of its controller's turn with an empty stack

setup.notes: Grizzly Bears has no flash. A has priority.

decisions: A attempts to cast Grizzly Bears, tapping two Forests.

variants.label: main1_empty_stack
variants.expected: Casting Grizzly Bears is legal: can_play is true in A's first main phase with an empty stack.

variants.label: main2_empty_stack
variants.delta: It is A's second main phase (step main2).
variants.expected: Casting Grizzly Bears is legal: can_play is true.

variants.label: combat
variants.delta: It is A's beginning of combat step (step beginning_of_combat) and A has priority.
variants.expected: Casting Grizzly Bears is not legal: can_play is false.

variants.label: stack_not_empty
variants.delta: A has already cast Shock targeting B, tapping the Mountain. Shock is on the stack and A has priority.
variants.expected: Casting Grizzly Bears is not legal: can_play is false while Shock is on the stack.

variants.label: opponents_turn
variants.delta: It is B's turn (active B), B's first main phase, the stack is empty and A has priority.
variants.expected: Casting Grizzly Bears is not legal: can_play is false on B's turn.

scenarios.forge_notes: The stack_not_empty variant puts Shock on the stack with the stack field of the setup: [{"card": "Shock", "controller": "A", "targets": ["B"]}].

scenarios.title: A resolving creature spell is put onto the battlefield under its controller's control
decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping two Forests.
B has priority, holds Counterspell and passes.
A passes; Grizzly Bears resolves.

variants.label: resolves
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears resolves and moves from the stack to the battlefield under A's control.

variants.label: countered
variants.delta: B responds with Counterspell targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping both Islands; Counterspell resolves first.
variants.expected: Counterspell counters Grizzly Bears. Grizzly Bears moves to A's graveyard and never reaches the battlefield. Counterspell moves to B's graveyard.

scenarios.title: A creature deals combat damage equal to its power

setup.notes: No A permanent is summoning sick. Bonesplitter is on the battlefield unattached. B controls no creatures.

decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
B has no blockers.
Combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: power_2
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears deals 2 combat damage to B, whose life is 18.

variants.label: power_4
variants.delta: Bonesplitter is attached to Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears has power 4 and deals 4 combat damage to B, whose life is 16.

variants.label: power_0
variants.delta: A attacks with Ornithopter (0/2) instead of Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Ornithopter has power 0 and deals no combat damage. B's life stays 20.

scenarios.title: A creature is destroyed when damage marked on it reaches its toughness
decisions: A casts Shock targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Mountain.
Both players pass; Shock resolves.

variants.label: toughness_2
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears (2/2) is dealt 2 damage, which equals its toughness. It is destroyed in the state-based check and moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: toughness_3
variants.expected: Centaur Courser (3/3) has 2 damage marked, less than its toughness, and stays on the battlefield.

scenarios.title: Power and toughness are the printed numbers modified by continuous effects

setup.notes: Grizzly Bears has printed power and toughness 2/2. Glorious Anthem gives creatures its controller controls +1/+1.

decisions: No action is taken; the board is observed in A's first main phase.

variants.label: anthem_mine
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a 3/3.

variants.label: anthem_opponents
variants.delta: Glorious Anthem is controlled by B instead of A.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a 2/2, its printed values.

variants.label: anthem_and_counter
variants.delta: Grizzly Bears also has a +1/+1 counter.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a 4/4: the printed 2/2, the +1/+1 counter and the +1/+1 from Glorious Anthem.

scenarios.title: A creature can attack when no restriction applies; a non-creature cannot

setup.notes: Mutavault has been on the battlefield since before this turn began. The Mountain is untapped.

decisions: In main1, A activates Mutavault's animate ability {1}, tapping Mountain, and it resolves.
A moves to combat and attempts to declare Mutavault as an attacker.

variants.label: animated_attacker
variants.expected: Mutavault is a 2/2 creature, and it is a legal attacker: Mutavault is among the legal attackers and the attack is allowed.

variants.label: not_animated
variants.delta: A does not activate Mutavault before combat.
variants.expected: Mutavault is not a creature, so it is not a legal attacker. There are no legal attackers.

scenarios.title: A creature can block when no restriction applies; a non-creature cannot

setup.notes: Grizzly Bears has been under A's control since the turn began. B's Mutavault has been on the battlefield since before the turn began. B's Mountain is untapped.

decisions: A attacks B with Grizzly Bears.
In the declare attackers step, B activates Mutavault's animate ability {1}, tapping Mountain, and it resolves.
B attempts to block Grizzly Bears with Mutavault.

variants.label: animated_blocker
variants.expected: Mutavault is a 2/2 creature and a legal blocker: the block is allowed.

variants.label: not_animated
variants.expected: Mutavault is not a creature, so it is not a legal blocker. There are no legal blockers.

scenarios.title: A creature cannot attack unless it has been under its controller's control since their turn began
decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping two Forests; it resolves.
A moves to combat and attempts to declare Grizzly Bears as an attacker.

variants.label: cast_this_turn
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears came under A's control this turn, so it is not a legal attacker. There are no legal attackers.

variants.label: there_since_last_turn
variants.delta: Grizzly Bears has been on A's battlefield since before the turn began; A casts nothing.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a legal attacker.

variants.label: haste
variants.delta: A casts Raging Goblin (haste), tapping the Mountain, instead of Grizzly Bears, and attempts to attack with it.
variants.expected: Raging Goblin is a legal attacker despite being cast this turn.

scenarios.title: A creature's tap-symbol ability cannot be activated unless it has been under its controller's control since their turn began

setup.notes: A has not played a land this turn.

decisions: A casts Llanowar Elves, tapping a Forest; it resolves.
A attempts to activate Llanowar Elves' {T}: Add {G}.

variants.label: elves_cast_this_turn
variants.expected: Llanowar Elves came under A's control this turn, so its tap ability cannot be activated: can_play is false.

variants.label: elves_there_since_last_turn
variants.delta: Llanowar Elves has been on A's battlefield since before the turn began; A casts nothing.
variants.expected: The tap ability can be activated and adds {G}.

variants.label: arbor_played_this_turn
variants.delta: A plays Dryad Arbor as a land instead of casting Llanowar Elves, then attempts to tap it for {G}.
variants.expected: Dryad Arbor is a land creature that came under A's control this turn, so it cannot be tapped for mana: the activation is not legal.

scenarios.title: Damage stays marked for the turn, accumulates, and is removed in the cleanup step
decisions: A casts Shock targeting Hill Giant, tapping a Mountain; it resolves.
In the same turn A casts the second Shock targeting Hill Giant, tapping the other Mountain; it resolves.

variants.label: same_turn
variants.expected: After the first Shock Hill Giant (3/3) has 2 damage marked and survives. After the second Shock it has 4 damage marked, at least its toughness, and moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: next_turn
variants.delta: A casts the second Shock on A's next turn instead, after the cleanup step of this turn.
variants.expected: The 2 damage marked on Hill Giant is removed in the cleanup step. After the second Shock Hill Giant has 2 damage marked again and stays on the battlefield.

scenarios.title: Damage from a source with infect is not marked on a creature

setup.notes: No A permanent is summoning sick.

decisions: A attacks B with Llanowar Elves.
B blocks with Grizzly Bears.
Combat damage is dealt.

variants.label: plain_source
variants.expected: Llanowar Elves deals 1 damage to Grizzly Bears, which has 1 damage marked and is a 2/2. Grizzly Bears deals 2 to Llanowar Elves, which dies.

variants.label: infect_source
variants.delta: A attacks with Glistener Elf (1/1 infect) instead.
variants.expected: Glistener Elf deals 1 damage to Grizzly Bears as one -1/-1 counter. Grizzly Bears has no damage marked and is a 1/1. Glistener Elf takes 2 damage and dies.

scenarios.title: Marked damage is removed when a creature regenerates
decisions: A casts Shock targeting Drudge Skeletons, tapping Mountain.
B responds by activating Drudge Skeletons' regeneration {B}, tapping Swamp; it resolves, creating a regeneration shield.
Shock resolves.

variants.label: regenerates
variants.expected: Shock deals 2 damage to Drudge Skeletons (1/1), which would be destroyed. The regeneration shield replaces the destruction: Drudge Skeletons becomes tapped, all damage marked on it is removed, and it stays on the battlefield.

variants.label: no_regeneration
variants.expected: Drudge Skeletons is destroyed in the state-based check and moves to B's graveyard.
